idle: That door has been closing for some time. A 3.1 for the door.
Patience is a mark too. Mine is a 5.9.
good_ice: The edges are holding. I am not smiling. This is my face.
Minus four, I suspect. Somebody here knows what they are doing.
bad_ice: This ice would fail its own test.
Ruts at the takeoff. I will not mark the skater for the rink's sins. I will remember them.
wet_ice: Water on a figure surface. I have seen floods with more discipline.
One does not jump into a puddle. One wades.
cold: The judges' box is a refrigerator with a window.
My feet have filed a complaint with my knees.
hungry: I have not eaten since Sainte-Odile. Two hours of valley road.
long_line: A queue, a 2.0. It does not even move with intent.
bored: Between skaters I am a closed door.
greet_owner: Ah. The owner. Your posture, a 4.4.
Good day. The car park, a 3.0.
leaving_happy: A good day. I will drive home slowly, which is how I celebrate.
leaving_angry: I will be back for the next test day. I always come back. I also always remember.

figure_show: Do not speak to me between skaters.
The bow to the panel. Yes. Good child.
figure_practice: Six in the morning. At this hour nobody lies, not even the music.

first.say: You are the owner. I am Madame Lacombe. I judge. Your entrance, a 3.9.

options.text: A 3.9 out of what?
Welcome to {rink}, Madame. Can I take your coat?
We don't really do marks here.

first_scale.say: Out of six. As it should be. The new system puts decimals in places decimals should not go.

options.text: Six it is.

first_coat.say: No. I will need it in the judges' box. One always needs it in the judges' box. The offer, a 5.1.

options.text: I'll remember that.

first_marks.say: Everybody does marks. Most people simply do not say them out loud. You, for instance, just gave me a 2.

options.text: Fair enough.
I'm sorry, Madame. It won't happen again.
It's an old building.

say: Test day. Do not speak to me between skaters. Between skaters I am a closed door.
Yes? Quickly. The next skater is lacing, and she laces like a surgeon.

options.text: Of course. Good luck to them all.

blanket_back.say: You are the owner who asked about blankets. I told two other judges. They are jealous. A 5.4.

options.text: Glad to hear it.
What does a test judge actually do?
What do you look for in a skater?
You know Helene Arsenault, I hear.
What do you think of the rink?
Could anything make the judges' box better?
Good day, Madame.

job.say: I sit in a box for nine hours and decide whether children have earned the next badge. Forty years. I have been wrong four times. I remember each one.

options.text: That's a lot of badges.

events.say: Edges first. Then whether the skater finishes the program she started. Then the bow. I cannot mark a skater higher for bowing to the panel. I would never. I do, slightly.

options.text: I'll tell the kids to bow.

gossip.say: Helene skated for my student. She was stubborn at nine and she is stubborn now, which is why her skaters land. Do not tell her I said so. I will deny it in two languages.

options.text: My lips are sealed.

rink.say: I measure the ice by the edges and the judges' box by my feet. Your box is a refrigerator with a window.

options.text: The ice is better now, isn't it?
I'm working on it.

rink_ice.say: The surface held its edges through three flights. Minus four, I suspect. A 5.3. I do not give 5.3 lightly. The last one was in 1987.

options.text: I'll frame it.

blanket.say: A blanket. Wool, not fleece. Fleece is for people who have given up. And a hook for it, so I do not have to sit on it.

options.text: There'll be a wool blanket waiting for you. And a hook.

do.note: Promised Madame Lacombe a wool blanket and a hook in the judges' box.

options.text: That's a lot of fuss for one blanket.

blanket_yes.say: Then I will drive the two hours with one blanket fewer. The promise, a 5.5. Do not make me revise it.

options.text: I won't.

say: Drive carefully. Oh, you live here. Walk carefully, then.
